body:
From the medialog spec (Myk's chat Fable, 2026-08-29) and a trap it hit in production: under
mask: drop, AN ANONYMOUS READER AND AN EMPTY STORE ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM OUTSIDE. The
synchronicity artifact rendered a masked-auth failure as a welcoming empty state - confidently
wrong in the way only a well-designed UI can be. H9's shape at the door: "nothing there" and
"nothing shown to YOU" must not be the same bytes.

Build a standing-introspection surface: a caller may ask who the door thinks they are and what
standing they hold. Two forms, one truth:
- An MCP tool `loam_whoami` (beside loam_docs in the roster): returns the resolved principal
  kind (operator | actor key | connector client | anonymous), and the standing the ground
  currently grants it - verbs with their prefixes, federate containers, roles where a user.
- The same answer over GraphQL (a `_standing` query field or REST sibling) so non-MCP clients
  ask the same question.
Read from the GROUND per request like every standing check (a revocation binds on the next
call). The ANONYMOUS answer is the point: it must say plainly that reads are masked and views
fold empty for this caller - the sentence the trap needed.

Acceptance criteria:
- (a) An operator token, an actor token, a connector session, and an anonymous caller each get
  a distinct, truthful answer naming their kind and standing; the anonymous answer names the
  masking. Verify: test/server/whoami.test.ts.
- (b) A revoked grant disappears from the answer on the very next call, no restart. Verify:
  the same suite, two-sided with a live sibling grant.
- (c) The tool appears in the MCP roster and its description teaches when to call it (the
  empty-vs-masked question). Verify: the same suite at the tools/list level.
title: loam_whoami: a caller may ask who the door thinks they are
